title: Standardized Intake & Routing for Pricing Concessions, Commitments, and Marketplace Invoices
creator: Aisha Nambiar
description: Goal: Create a single, repeatable intake and routing framework for non-bug customer requests related to pricing concessions, commitment contracts, invoicing exceptions, and marketplace credit allocations. The framework should: 1) surface necessary business context for fast decisions, 2) score requests by revenue & risk to prioritize engineering and finance effort, 3) route to the correct team (Billing Ops / Sales Engineering / Legal / Finance / Dedicated PM), and 4) provide a minimum viable automation to accelerate triage and reduce manual handoffs. Scope: applies to all inbound customer pricing/billing requests that are not technical platform bugs (e.g., contract changes, invoice re-issues, marketplace fee adjustments, commitment credit allocation exceptions). Out of scope: platform incidents, chargeback engineering tasks that originate from internal cost allocation fixes, and bespoke legal contract negotiation flows which remain with Sales. Success metrics: - Median first response time <= 48 hours for P1/P0 pricing requests - % of routing decisions handled without manual PM intervention >= 60% within 3 months - Reduction in time-to-resolution for standard invoice reissue requests from median 7 days to <= 3 days - Number of escalations to legal per month for small invoice adjustments < 5 Proposed scoring model (two-axis): - Revenue Impact (0-10): delta to ARR / one-time credit value mapped to bands - Operational Risk & Compliance (0-10): regulatory or tax implications, required GL changes - Implementation Complexity (0-5): effort estimate for ENG/Finance to implement - Customer SLAs / Sales Tier multiplier (x1.0 - x2.0) Decision: score = (Revenue Impact + Operational Risk) * SalesTierMultiplier - Implementation Complexity as a gating label Routing matrix (example): - Score >= 15 => Route to Revenue & Billing Ops + Finance review + PM allocation - Score 8-14 => Route to Billing Ops with Sales Eng oversight and standardized approval flow - Score < 8 => Self-service playbook / Finance checklist; auto-approve for credits < $5000 and non-compliance risk low Required intake fields (minimum): - Customer name & contract ID - Request type (commitment amendment / invoice reissue / marketplace credit / pricing concession) - Requested outcome and justification - Dollar value impact (estimate) - Deadline / customer SLA - Sales rep and AE contact - Relevant contract clause / invoice number - Attach supporting docs (signed amendment, dispute ticket) Automation opportunities: - Web form + Linear webhook to create pre-populated ticket with score computed by serverless function - Auto-routing labels in Linear and email to stakeholders based on score bands - A small Google Sheet / BigQuery ETL to compute dollar exposures for quick scoring Data needs & queries: - Quick SQL to estimate remaining commitment balance by contract_id: SELECT contract_id, total_committed_usd, consumed_usd, (total_committed_usd - consumed_usd) as remaining FROM billing.commitments WHERE contract_id = '<<contract_id>>'; Stakeholders: - Billing Ops (primary) - Finance (approver) - Sales (request origin / customer liaison) - Legal (compliance review for tax/contract changes) - Engineering (for invoicing system changes) Next steps: 1) Draft intake form and Confluence playbook v0.1 (owner: Marco) 2) Run 2-week pilot with Billing Ops and 12 recent historical requests to validate scoring thresholds 3) Implement Linear webhook + serverless scorer for automated label assignment 4) Iterate on playbook and publish to internal docs Acceptance criteria: - Playbook published with clear routing table and sample completed ticket - Pilot results show >= 50% correct routing vs manual decisions - Linear tickets created from web intake include pre-scored label and required attachments
